claim: The zebrafish genome encodes a single, well-conserved orthologue of ZBTB24.
source: The zebrafish genome encodes a single, well-conserved orthologue of ZBTB24, which we mutated using TAL effector nucleases (TALENs) (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by reference to figures showing the protein structure and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The zbtb24mk22 allele is a 7.9 kb deletion that eliminates coding sequence between exons 2 and 5.
source: The recovered 7.9 kb deletion allele (zbtb24mk22; here after referred to as zbtb24Δ), eliminates coding sequence between exons 2 and 5 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The deletion size and location are explicitly stated and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Animals homozygous for zbtb24Δ lack detectable zbtb24 transcripts.
source: Animals that were homozygous for this deletion lacked detectable zbtb24 transcripts, suggesting zbtb24Δ is a null allele (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D shows absence of transcripts in mutants.

claim: zbtb24Δ is a null allele.
source: Animals that were homozygous for this deletion lacked detectable zbtb24 transcripts, suggesting zbtb24Δ is a null allele (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of detectable transcripts.

claim: Zbtb24Δ/Δ embryos are born to heterozygous parents at expected Mendelian ratios.
source: Zbtb24Δ/Δ embryos were born to heterozygous parents at the expected Mendelian ratios and had no obvious morphological abnormalities during the first two weeks of development (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on observed breeding outcomes.

claim: Zbtb24Δ/Δ embryos have no obvious morphological abnormalities during the first two weeks of development.
source: Zbtb24Δ/Δ embryos were born to heterozygous parents at the expected Mendelian ratios and had no obvious morphological abnormalities during the first two weeks of development (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 1C showing similar appearance to wild-type.

claim: By 3-4 weeks post fertilization, zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant zebrafish are smaller than wild-type siblings raised under identical conditions.
source: Consistent with the small stature observed in ICF syndrome, by 3–4 weeks post fertilization (wpf), zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant zebrafish were smaller than wild-type siblings raised under identical conditions, and this size reduction persisted into adulthood (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by measurements shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: The size reduction in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants persists into adulthood.
source: Consistent with the small stature observed in ICF syndrome, by 3–4 weeks post fertilization (wpf), zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant zebrafish were smaller than wild-type siblings raised under identical conditions, and this size reduction persisted into adulthood (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1D-F showing continued size differences.

claim: Adult zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants exhibit facial anomalies characterized by elongation of the snout.
source: As adults, zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants exhibited facial anomalies that were characterized by a quantifiable elongation of the snout (Figure 1G–H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and quantified in Figure 1G-H.

claim: zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants show evidence of hypogammaglobulinemia in the presence of normal lymphoid cell numbers.
source: We also noted evidence of hypogammagloblulinemia in the presence of normal lymphoid cell numbers, which is an immunological hallmark of ICF syndrome (Figure 1I–J).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1I-J showing reduced immunoglobulin expression but normal lymphoid cell counts.

claim: Hypogammaglobulinemia in the presence of normal lymphoid cell numbers is an immunological hallmark of ICF syndrome.
source: We also noted evidence of hypogammagloblulinemia in the presence of normal lymphoid cell numbers, which is an immunological hallmark of ICF syndrome (Figure 1I–J).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ICF syndrome.

claim: Significant death was noted among homozygous mutants at 4 months of age.
source: Significant death was noted among homozygous mutants at 4 months of age and fewer than 10% of zbtb24Δ/Δ animals survived beyond 8 months (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the survival curve in Figure 1K.

claim: Fewer than 10% of zbtb24Δ/Δ animals survived beyond 8 months.
source: Significant death was noted among homozygous mutants at 4 months of age and fewer than 10% of zbtb24Δ/Δ animals survived beyond 8 months (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the Kaplan-Meier curve in Figure 1K.

claim: Attempts to recover fertilized embryos by intercrossing or outcrossing zbtb24Δ/Δ adults were unsuccessful.
source: Attempts to recover fertilized embryos by intercrossing or outcrossing zbtb24Δ/Δ adults were unsuccessful, suggesting that animals were sterile (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by breeding outcome data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: zbtb24Δ/Δ animals are sterile.
source: Attempts to recover fertilized embryos by intercrossing or outcrossing zbtb24Δ/Δ adults were unsuccessful, suggesting that animals were sterile (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is inferred from unsuccessful breeding attempts.

claim: Gonadal morphology in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants appears overtly similar to wild-type siblings in histological sections.
source: Gonadal morphology in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants appeared overtly similar to wild-type siblings in histological sections (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in histological images in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B-C.

claim: Testes size is severely reduced in zbtb24 mutants.
source: However, testes size and sperm count were severely reduced in zbtb24 mutants, providing one potential explanation for impaired male fertility (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and quantified in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D-E.

claim: Sperm count is severely reduced in zbtb24 mutants.
source: However, testes size and sperm count were severely reduced in zbtb24 mutants, providing one potential explanation for impaired male fertility (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and quantified in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F-G.

claim: Reduced testes size and sperm count provide one potential explanation for impaired male fertility in zbtb24 mutants.
source: However, testes size and sperm count were severely reduced in zbtb24 mutants, providing one potential explanation for impaired male fertility (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D–G).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observed data.

claim: Similar ICF-like phenotypes were observed in zebrafish homozygous for a second independently-isolated mutant allele of zbtb24 (zbtb24mk19).
source: Similar ICF-like phenotypes were observed in zebrafish that were homozygous for a second independently-isolated mutant allele of zbtb24 (zbtb24mk19) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: zbtb24 homozygous mutant zebrafish are a faithful animal model of ICF syndrome phenotypes.
source: Taken together, these findings identify zbtb24 homozygous mutant zebrafish as a faithful animal model of ICF syndrome phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multiple phenotypic similarities observed.

claim: Pericentromeric satellite type-1 (Sat1) repeats are found on all zebrafish chromosomes.
source: Pericentromeric satellite type-1 (Sat1) repeats are found on all zebrafish chromosomes and comprise 5–8% of the zebrafish genome (Phillips and Reed, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to prior work.

claim: Sat1 repeats comprise 5-8% of the zebrafish genome.
source: Pericentromeric satellite type-1 (Sat1) repeats are found on all zebrafish chromosomes and comprise 5–8% of the zebrafish genome (Phillips and Reed, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to prior work.

claim: Sat1 sequences from wild-type adults are resistant to digestion with the methylation sensitive restriction enzyme HpyCH4IV.
source: As expected, we found that Sat1 sequences from wild-type adults were resistant to digestion with the methylation sensitive restriction enzyme HpyCH4IV, indicating that these pericentromeric repeats were heavily methylated.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on experimental results.

claim: Pericentromeric repeats in wild-type adults are heavily methylated.
source: As expected, we found that Sat1 sequences from wild-type adults were resistant to digestion with the methylation sensitive restriction enzyme HpyCH4IV, indicating that these pericentromeric repeats were heavily methylated.
evidence: This is inferred from resistance to methylation-sensitive enzyme digestion.

claim: Sat1 sequences from zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults are readily digested with HpyCH4IV.
source: In contrast to wildtype, Sat1 sequences from zbtb24Δ/Δ and zbtb24mk19/mk19 mutant adults were readily digested with HpyCH4IV, indicating extensive loss of methylation at these repeats (Figure 2A–B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Southern blot data in Figure 2A-B.

claim: zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults show extensive loss of methylation at Sat1 repeats.
source: In contrast to wildtype, Sat1 sequences from zbtb24Δ/Δ and zbtb24mk19/mk19 mutant adults were readily digested with HpyCH4IV, indicating extensive loss of methylation at these repeats (Figure 2A–B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is inferred from sensitivity to methylation-sensitive enzyme digestion.

claim: Comparable Sat1 methylation deficiencies were observed when DNA was isolated from dissected adult brain, skin, muscle and fin.
source: Comparable Sat1 methylation deficiencies were observed when DNA was isolated from dissected adult brain, skin, muscle and fin, suggesting that these sequences were similarly hypomethylated in most adult somatic tissues (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Southern blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Sat1 sequences are similarly hypomethylated in most adult somatic tissues in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Comparable Sat1 methylation deficiencies were observed when DNA was isolated from dissected adult brain, skin, muscle and fin, suggesting that these sequences were similarly hypomethylated in most adult somatic tissues (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is inferred from comparable methylation deficiencies across multiple tissues.

claim: Methylation levels at Sat1 repeats appear normal in remaining sperm extracted from zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults.
source: Methylation levels at Sat1 repeats appeared normal in remaining sperm extracted from zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults, suggesting methylation loss may be restricted to somatic tissues (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Southern blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Methylation loss at Sat1 repeats may be restricted to somatic tissues in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Methylation levels at Sat1 repeats appeared normal in remaining sperm extracted from zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults, suggesting methylation loss may be restricted to somatic tissues (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is inferred from normal methylation in sperm but not somatic tissues.

claim: Pericentromeric methylation loss in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants is progressive.
source: Somewhat unexpectedly, we found that pericentromeric methylation loss in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants was progressive.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on time-course experiments.

claim: Extensive hypomethylation of Sat1 sequences was detected in zbtb24Δ/Δ adults but not in mutants at 1 wpf.
source: While extensive hypomethylation of Sat1 sequences was detected in adults lacking zbtb24, similar hypomethylation was not observed in mutants at 1 wpf (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Southern blot data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: At 2 wpf, zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants exhibit roughly 3-fold increases in HpyCH4IV digestion.
source: At 2 wpf, zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants exhibited roughly 3-fold increases in HpyCH4IV digestion, and sensitivity to digestion became increasingly pronounced in older animals (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and quantified in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Sensitivity to HpyCH4IV digestion becomes increasingly pronounced in older zbtb24Δ/Δ animals.
source: At 2 wpf, zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants exhibited roughly 3-fold increases in HpyCH4IV digestion, and sensitivity to digestion became increasingly pronounced in older animals (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: By 32 weeks, Sat1 sequences from zbtb24 mutants exhibit a 23-fold increase in HpyCH4IV digestion compared to wildtype.
source: By 32 weeks, Sat1 sequences from zbtb24 mutants exhibited a 23-fold increase in HpyCH4IV digestion compared to wildtype, suggesting a greater than 95% reduction in methylation of these repetitive sequence blocks.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on quantification of Southern blot data.

claim: By 32 weeks, zbtb24 mutants show a greater than 95% reduction in methylation of Sat1 sequences.
source: By 32 weeks, Sat1 sequences from zbtb24 mutants exhibited a 23-fold increase in HpyCH4IV digestion compared to wildtype, suggesting a greater than 95% reduction in methylation of these repetitive sequence blocks.
evidence: This is inferred from the 23-fold increase in digestion.

claim: Histone H3 lysine nine trimethylation levels are unaffected at Sat1 sequences in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults.
source: Histone H3 lysine nine trimethylation levels were unaffected at Sat1 sequences in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: ERRBS analysis revealed a strong correlation between genome wide 5mC levels in wild-type and zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults (Pearson's correlation value of 0.928).
source: Our analysis revealed a strong correlation between genome wide 5mC levels in wild-type and zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults (Pearson's correlation value of 0.928), although overall methylation levels appeared reduced by ~10% at all methylated sequence features in mutants (Figure 2E–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Overall methylation levels are reduced by ~10% at all methylated sequence features in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants.
source: Our analysis revealed a strong correlation between genome wide 5mC levels in wild-type and zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults (Pearson's correlation value of 0.928), although overall methylation levels appeared reduced by ~10% at all methylated sequence features in mutants (Figure 2E–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Reductions in methylation in zbtb24 mutants consist primarily of small-magnitude changes in 5mC across the genome.
source: Reductions consisted primarily of small-magnitude changes in 5mC across the genome, with only 1.3% (13,205) of examined CpG dinucleotides exhibiting methylation differences of greater than 20%.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on ERRBS analysis.

claim: Only 1.3% (13,205) of examined CpG dinucleotides exhibit methylation differences of greater than 20% in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Reductions consisted primarily of small-magnitude changes in 5mC across the genome, with only 1.3% (13,205) of examined CpG dinucleotides exhibiting methylation differences of greater than 20%.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on ERRBS analysis.

claim: At a threshold of 20% change (p-value<0.01), only 55 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified between wild-type and zbtb24Δ/Δ adults.
source: Consistent with these findings, at a threshold of 20% change (p-value<0.01), only 55 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified between wild-type and zbtb24Δ/Δ adults (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text based on ERRBS analysis.

claim: All tested endogenous retroviruses and transposable elements were similarly resistant to digestion in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults and wild-type siblings.
source: Methylation levels at endogenous retroviruses and other transposable elements were also examined by methylation sensitive restriction digest. All tested elements were similarly resistant to digestion in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant adults and wild-type siblings (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Southern blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Pericentromeres are a predominant site of methylation loss in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that pericentromeres are a predominant site of methylation loss in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ERRBS and Southern blot data showing minimal changes elsewhere.

claim: RNA-seq identified 58 genes that were downregulated by more than 2-fold in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae at 2 wpf.
source: RNA-seq identified 58 genes that were downregulated by more than 2-fold in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae at 2 wpf, while 119 were upregulated by 2-fold or more (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: RNA-seq identified 119 genes that were upregulated by 2-fold or more in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae at 2 wpf.
source: RNA-seq identified 58 genes that were downregulated by more than 2-fold in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae at 2 wpf, while 119 were upregulated by 2-fold or more (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: No gene enrichment signature was observed among downregulated genes in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae at 2 wpf.
source: No gene enrichment signature was observed among downregulated genes.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Roughly 30% of upregulated genes in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae at 2 wpf are associated with activation of the innate immune system.
source: However, roughly 30% of upregulated genes were associated with activation of the innate immune system.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Upregulated transcripts in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae include those associated with interferon stimulated genes (ISGs) and inflammatory cytokines.
source: In particular, we noted that upregulated transcripts included those associated with interferon stimulated genes (ISGs) and inflammatory cytokines (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the heatmap in Figure 3B.

claim: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) identified significant enrichment of genes involved in viral response in zbtb24Δ/Δ larvae.
source: Consistent with these observations, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) identified significant enrichment of genes involved in viral response, a key function of innate immune pathways (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Upregulation of ISGs was observed in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants by qRT-PCR at 3 wpf.
source: Upregulation of ISGs was also observed in zbtb24Δ/Δ and zbtb24mk19/mk19 mutants by qRT-PCR at 3 wpf, whereas the same genes were expressed at wild-type levels at 1 wpf (Figure 3D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ISGs are expressed at wild-type levels in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants at 1 wpf.
source: Upregulation of ISGs was also observed in zbtb24Δ/Δ and zbtb24mk19/mk19 mutants by qRT-PCR at 3 wpf, whereas the same genes were expressed at wild-type levels at 1 wpf (Figure 3D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: No immune-related genes were found within 100 kb of identified DMRs.
source: No immune-related genes (and only one gene differentially upregulated in the RNA-Seq) were found within 100 kb of identified DMRs, suggesting that direct loss of methylation at these sequences was unlikely to cause the response (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Direct loss of methylation at DMRs is unlikely to cause the immune response in zbtb24 mutants.
source: No immune-related genes (and only one gene differentially upregulated in the RNA-Seq) were found within 100 kb of identified DMRs, suggesting that direct loss of methylation at these sequences was unlikely to cause the response (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of immune genes near DMRs.

claim: Global methylation depletion using 5-azacytidine results in upregulation of immune response genes.
source: Consistent with previous studies, we found that global methylation depletion using the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor 5-azacytidine also resulted in upregulation of immune response genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to previous studies and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Homozygous mutation of myd88 has little impact on expression of ISGs in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants.
source: Introduction of myd88 or sting mutations had little impact on expression of these ISGs, as similar transcript levels were detected in zbtb24Δ/Δ single mutant animals compared to myd88hu3568/hu3568; zbtb24Δ/Δ or stingmk30/mk30; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Homozygous mutation of sting has little impact on expression of ISGs in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutants.
source: Introduction of myd88 or sting mutations had little impact on expression of these ISGs, as similar transcript levels were detected in zbtb24Δ/Δ single mutant animals compared to myd88hu3568/hu3568; zbtb24Δ/Δ or stingmk30/mk30; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TLR and cGAS PRRs have limited roles in mediating the interferon response in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Sustained ISG expression in these double mutants suggests limited roles for TLR and cGAS PRRs in mediating the interferon response in zbtb24 mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of myd88 and sting mutations.

claim: Mutation of mavs suppresses stat1b and irf7 upregulation in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant animals.
source: In contrast to myd88 and sting, mutation of mavs suppressed stat1b and irf7 upregulation in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant animals.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: Expression levels of irf7 and stat1b are reduced 2- and 4-fold respectively in mavsmk28/mk28; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants compared to zbtb24Δ/Δ single mutants.
source: Expression levels of irf7 and stat1b were reduced 2- and 4-fold respectively in mavsmk28/mk28; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants when compared to zbtb24Δ/Δ single mutant zebrafish, indicating a requirement for mavs in the upregulation of these ISGs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: mavs is required for the upregulation of ISGs in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Expression levels of irf7 and stat1b were reduced 2- and 4-fold respectively in mavsmk28/mk28; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants when compared to zbtb24Δ/Δ single mutant zebrafish, indicating a requirement for mavs in the upregulation of these ISGs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is inferred from the suppression of ISG upregulation in mavs mutants.

claim: RLR signaling is implicated in the activation of the innate immune system in zbtb24 mutants.
source: This finding implicates RLR signaling in the activation of the innate immune system in zbtb24 mutants and suggests a cytosolic RNA trigger for the response.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for mavs, which is downstream of RLRs.

claim: A cytosolic RNA trigger is suggested for the immune response in zbtb24 mutants.
source: This finding implicates RLR signaling in the activation of the innate immune system in zbtb24 mutants and suggests a cytosolic RNA trigger for the response.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for mavs and RLR signaling.

claim: Strong derepression of Sat1 RNA from hypomethylated pericentromeres was noted in zbtb24 mutant adults.
source: Consistent with this model, strong derepression of Sat1 RNA from hypomethylated pericentromeres was noted in zbtb24 mutant adults (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), whereas transcripts for other dispersed repetitive elements remained unchanged between mutants and wildtype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Northern blot data in Figure 5A.

claim: Transcripts for dispersed repetitive elements remain unchanged between zbtb24 mutants and wildtype.
source: Consistent with this model, strong derepression of Sat1 RNA from hypomethylated pericentromeres was noted in zbtb24 mutant adults (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), whereas transcripts for other dispersed repetitive elements remained unchanged between mutants and wildtype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Increases in Sat1 transcripts correlate with levels of irf7 expression in adult zebrafish (r = 0.77).
source: Increases in Sat1 transcripts correlated with levels of irf7 expression in adult zebrafish (r = 0.77), and upregulation of Sat1 transcripts coincided with the window of ISG induction during development (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Upregulation of Sat1 transcripts coincides with the window of ISG induction during development.
source: Increases in Sat1 transcripts correlated with levels of irf7 expression in adult zebrafish (r = 0.77), and upregulation of Sat1 transcripts coincided with the window of ISG induction during development (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Both sense and antisense Sat1 transcripts are detected in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Both sense and antisense transcripts were detected in mutants using TAG-aided sense/antisense transcript detection (TASA-TD) strand-specific PCR (Henke et al., 2015), suggesting the potential for derepressed Sat1 transcripts to form double stranded RNAs (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Derepressed Sat1 transcripts have the potential to form double stranded RNAs.
source: Both sense and antisense transcripts were detected in mutants using TAG-aided sense/antisense transcript detection (TASA-TD) strand-specific PCR (Henke et al., 2015), suggesting the potential for derepressed Sat1 transcripts to form double stranded RNAs (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This is inferred from the presence of both sense and antisense transcripts.

claim: Co-injection of sense and antisense Sat1 RNA is sufficient to cause 2 to 4-fold upregulation in expression of ISGs in wild-type embryos.
source: Co-injection of sense and antisense Sat1 RNA was sufficient to reproducibly cause a 2 to 4-fold upregulation in expression of these ISGs, whereas combined injection of sense and antisense control transcripts encoding a fragment of zebrafish β-actin or GFP had no effect on expression of these genes (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Combined injection of sense and antisense control transcripts encoding β-actin or GFP has no effect on ISG expression.
source: Co-injection of sense and antisense Sat1 RNA was sufficient to reproducibly cause a 2 to 4-fold upregulation in expression of these ISGs, whereas combined injection of sense and antisense control transcripts encoding a fragment of zebrafish β-actin or GFP had no effect on expression of these genes (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Lower level upregulation of some ISGs was noted when sense or antisense Sat1 transcripts were individually injected.
source: Lower level upregulation of some, but not all ISGs was noted when sense or antisense Sat1 transcripts were individually injected into the embryo, suggesting that the response was primarily triggered by formation of Sat1 dsRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The immune response is primarily triggered by formation of Sat1 dsRNA.
source: Lower level upregulation of some, but not all ISGs was noted when sense or antisense Sat1 transcripts were individually injected into the embryo, suggesting that the response was primarily triggered by formation of Sat1 dsRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the stronger response to co-injection of sense and antisense transcripts.

claim: Derepression of Sat1 transcripts is functionally linked to activation of the innate immune response in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Collectively, these results functionally link the derepression of Sat1 transcripts to the activation of the innate immune response in zbtb24 mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the injection experiments showing Sat1 RNA can trigger the response.

claim: Homozygous mutation of mda5 is sufficient to restore stat1b and irf7 expression to wild-type levels in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant larvae.
source: Homozygous mutation of mda5 was sufficient to restore stat1b and irf7 expression to wild-type levels in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant larvae, suggesting that Mda5 is the primary PPR required for the response (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Mda5 is the primary PPR required for the immune response in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Homozygous mutation of mda5 was sufficient to restore stat1b and irf7 expression to wild-type levels in zbtb24Δ/Δ mutant larvae, suggesting that Mda5 is the primary PPR required for the response (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of ISG expression in mda5; zbtb24 double mutants.

claim: A broad panel of ISGs that show elevated expression in zbtb24 single mutants are no longer upregulated in mda5mk29/mk29; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants.
source: This requirement was further validated by RNA-seq, which revealed that a broad panel of ISGs that showed elevated expression in zbtb24 single mutants were no longer upregulated in mda5mk29/mk29; zbtb24Δ/Δ double mutants (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the heatmap in Figure 6C.

claim: Loss of Zbtb24 function causes hypomethylation of pericentromeric Sat1 repeats.
source: Loss of Zbtb24 function causes hypomethylation of pericentromeric Sat1 repeats, which leads to derepression of associated Sat1 transcripts.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Hypomethylation of pericentromeric Sat1 repeats leads to derepression of associated Sat1 transcripts.
source: Loss of Zbtb24 function causes hypomethylation of pericentromeric Sat1 repeats, which leads to derepression of associated Sat1 transcripts.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pericentromeric transcripts are recognized by the RNA helicase Mda5.
source: These pericentromeric transcripts are recognized by the RNA helicase Mda5 which signals through Mavs and Irf7 to upregulate ISGs.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings from the genetic experiments.

claim: Mda5 signals through Mavs and Irf7 to upregulate ISGs.
source: These pericentromeric transcripts are recognized by the RNA helicase Mda5 which signals through Mavs and Irf7 to upregulate ISGs.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings from the genetic experiments.

claim: Derepression of transcripts from hypomethylated pericentromeres triggers activation of the innate immune system through the Mda5/Mavs viral RNA recognition pathway.
source: Taken together, these results support a model in which derepression of transcripts from hypomethylated pericentromeres triggers activation of the innate immune system through the Mda5/Mavs viral RNA recognition pathway (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all the experimental findings.

claim: Pericentromeric RNA can act as a trigger of autoimmunity.
source: These findings identify roles for pericentromeric RNA as a trigger of autoimmunity and reveal important functions for pericentromeric methylation in suppressing the generation of these immunostimulatory transcripts.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings that pericentromeric RNA triggers an immune response.

claim: Pericentromeric methylation has important functions in suppressing the generation of immunostimulatory transcripts.
source: These findings identify roles for pericentromeric RNA as a trigger of autoimmunity and reveal important functions for pericentromeric methylation in suppressing the generation of these immunostimulatory transcripts.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that loss of methylation leads to transcript derepression and immune activation.

claim: Induction of the innate immune system is one of the earliest in vivo consequences of pericentromeric methylation loss.
source: Based on these results, we propose that induction of the innate immune system is one of the earliest in vivo consequences of pericentromeric methylation loss.
evidence: This is proposed based on the timing of ISG upregulation relative to other phenotypes.

claim: zbtb24 mutant zebrafish provide an important new resource for understanding ICF disease etiology during juvenile and adult life stages.
source: Given that previous attempts to model ICF syndrome have resulted in perinatal or embryonic lethality (Geiman et al., 2001; Ueda et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2016), this zebrafish model provides an important new resource for understanding ICF disease etiology during juvenile and adult life stages.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion with citations to prior work showing lethality in other models.

claim: Previous attempts to model ICF syndrome in mice resulted in perinatal or embryonic lethality.
source: Given that previous attempts to model ICF syndrome have resulted in perinatal or embryonic lethality (Geiman et al., 2001; Ueda et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2016), this zebrafish model provides an important new resource for understanding ICF disease etiology during juvenile and adult life stages.
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: zbtb24 mutant zebrafish will be useful for understanding immunoglobulin deficiency phenotypes.
source: In particular, zbtb24 mutant zebrafish will be useful for understanding phenotypes such as immunoglobulin deficiency, which have not been observed in mouse models and are difficult to study in cell culture systems.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application of the model.

claim: Immunoglobulin deficiency has not been observed in mouse models of ICF syndrome.
source: In particular, zbtb24 mutant zebrafish will be useful for understanding phenotypes such as immunoglobulin deficiency, which have not been observed in mouse models and are difficult to study in cell culture systems.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: The general methylation landscape in human ICF syndrome and in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish is similar.
source: Nonetheless, ERRBS analysis suggested that the general methylation landscape in human ICF syndrome and in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish is similar.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from comparing ERRBS data to published ICF patient data.

claim: Methylome analysis of primary blood from ICF patients identified methylation changes of greater than 20% at roughly 3% of examined CpG dinucleotides.
source: Methylome analysis of primary blood from ICF patients identified methylation changes of greater than 20% at roughly 3% of examined CpG dinucleotides.
evidence: This is stated with implicit reference to published ICF patient data.

claim: Significant changes in methylation of retroviruses and other dispersed repeats were not observed in ICF patients.
source: Significant changes in methylation of retroviruses and other dispersed repeats were not observed in these patients (Velasco et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to prior work.

claim: The low-level methylation changes outside of the pericentromeres observed in ICF syndrome and zbtb24 mutants raise the possibility that zbtb24 may have additional modest roles in maintaining methylation at non pericentromeric sequences.
source: The low-level methylation changes outside of the pericentromeres observed in ICF syndrome and our mutants raise the possibility that zbtb24 may have additional modest roles in maintaining methylation at non pericentromeric sequences.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the observed data.

claim: CpG poor sequences can be under represented in ERRBS analysis.
source: One important caveat of ERRBS analysis is that CpG poor sequences can be under represented, leaving open the possibility that additional DMRs in CpG poor regions of the genome were overlooked by our approach.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of the ERRBS method.

claim: Additional DMRs in CpG poor regions of the genome may have been overlooked by ERRBS.
source: One important caveat of ERRBS analysis is that CpG poor sequences can be under represented, leaving open the possibility that additional DMRs in CpG poor regions of the genome were overlooked by our approach.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility given the limitations of ERRBS.

claim: The progressive loss of 5mC in somatic tissues between larval and adult stages implicates Zbtb24 in regulating the long-term maintenance of methylation at pericentromeric repeats.
source: The progressive loss of 5mC we observe in somatic tissues between larval and adult stages implicates Zbtb24 in regulating the long-term maintenance of methylation at pericentromeric repeats.
evidence: This is inferred from the progressive nature of methylation loss.

claim: The onset of methylation loss around 2 wpf partly reflects the need to deplete maternally loaded zbtb24 prior to unmasking of the zbtb24 mutant phenotype.
source: Rather, we speculate that the onset of methylation loss at this stage partly reflects the need to deplete maternally loaded zbtb24 prior to unmasking of the zbtb24 mutant phenotype and partly reflects the culmination of minor methylation losses due to lower fidelity maintenance over many rounds of cell division.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The onset of methylation loss around 2 wpf partly reflects the culmination of minor methylation losses due to lower fidelity maintenance over many rounds of cell division.
source: Rather, we speculate that the onset of methylation loss at this stage partly reflects the need to deplete maternally loaded zbtb24 prior to unmasking of the zbtb24 mutant phenotype and partly reflects the culmination of minor methylation losses due to lower fidelity maintenance over many rounds of cell division.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The onset of ICF-like growth defects in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish emerged in the weeks following Sat1 methylation loss.
source: We note that the onset of ICF-like growth defects in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish emerged in the weeks following Sat1 methylation loss.
evidence: This is stated based on the temporal relationship between methylation loss and phenotype onset.

claim: In at least one case of ICF syndrome type 2, growth reductions and immunodeficiency were reported to develop with age.
source: In at least one case of ICF syndrome type 2, growth reductions and immunodeficiency were also reported to develop with age, raising the possibility that similar progressive methylation loss may impact ICF etiology in humans (von Bernuth et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a case report.

claim: Similar progressive methylation loss may impact ICF etiology in humans.
source: In at least one case of ICF syndrome type 2, growth reductions and immunodeficiency were also reported to develop with age, raising the possibility that similar progressive methylation loss may impact ICF etiology in humans (von Bernuth et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on the zebrafish findings and a human case report.

claim: It is possible that Zbtb24 functions in both maintenance and establishment of pericentromeric methylation.
source: It is also possible that Zbtb24 functions in both maintenance and establishment of pericentromeric methylation, but that requirements for establishment are masked by maternally deposited RNA in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish lines.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility.

claim: Requirements for Zbtb24 in establishment of pericentromeric methylation may be masked by maternally deposited RNA in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish lines.
source: It is also possible that Zbtb24 functions in both maintenance and establishment of pericentromeric methylation, but that requirements for establishment are masked by maternally deposited RNA in zbtb24 mutant zebrafish lines.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility to explain why establishment defects are not observed.

claim: zbtb24 homozygous mutant zebrafish are sterile, preventing the generation of maternal-zygotic mutants.
source: Unfortunately, zbtb24 homozygous mutant zebrafish are sterile, preventing the generation of the maternal-zygotic mutants required to address this question.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the model.

claim: Previous studies have suggested that ZBTB24 is a transcription factor that may act to regulate DNA methylation through transcriptional control of the ICF gene CDCA7.
source: Previous studies have suggested that ZBTB24 is a transcription factor that may act to regulate DNA methylation through transcriptional control of the ICF gene CDCA7 (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to prior work.

claim: Near complete loss of cdca7 expression is observed in zbtb24 mutants.
source: Consistent with this model, we observe near complete loss of cdca7 expression in zbtb24 mutants in our RNA-seq data set and by qRT-PCR (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: A recent study proposed that ZBTB24 binding might be directly involved in recruiting DNMT3B to promote gene body methylation through recognition of AGGTCCTGGCAG motifs in human cells.
source: A more recent study in cultured human cells proposed that ZBTB24 binding might be directly involved in recruiting DNMT3B to promote gene body methylation through recognition of AGGTCCTGGCAG motifs in human cells (Thompson et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to prior work.

claim: The AGGTCCTGGCAG motif was not found in the promoter or gene body of zebrafish cdca7 or at Sat1 sequences.
source: Analysis using Find Individual Motif Occurrences (FIMO) (Grant et al., 2011), did not reveal this motif in the promoter or gene body of zebrafish cdca7 or at Sat1 sequences.
evidence: This is stated based on motif analysis.

claim: Activation of interferon signaling is one of the earliest in vivo consequences of pericentromeric hypomethylation.
source: In the current study, we take advantage of the progressive Sat1 methylation loss in zbtb24 mutants to identify activation of interferon signaling as one of the earliest in vivo consequences of pericentromeric hypomethylation.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: The interferon response phenotype in zbtb24 mutants cannot be attributed to defects in adaptive immunity.
source: This phenotype cannot be attributed to defects in adaptive immunity, as the zebrafish adaptive immune system is not functional until roughly 4 wpf (Trede et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with a citation about zebrafish immune system development.

claim: The zebrafish adaptive immune system is not functional until roughly 4 wpf.
source: This phenotype cannot be attributed to defects in adaptive immunity, as the zebrafish adaptive immune system is not functional until roughly 4 wpf (Trede et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to prior work.

claim: Induction of an interferon response has been reported in cancer cell lines treated with 5-azacytidine.
source: Induction of an interferon response has been reported in the context of global hypomethylation in cancer cell lines treated with the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor 5-azacytidine and in zebrafish mutated for the maintenance DNA methyltransferase machinery (Chernyavskaya et al., 2017; Chiappinelli et al., 2015; Roulois et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Induction of an interferon response has been reported in zebrafish mutated for the maintenance DNA methyltransferase machinery.
source: Induction of an interferon response has been reported in the context of global hypomethylation in cancer cell lines treated with the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor 5-azacytidine and in zebrafish mutated for the maintenance DNA methyltransferase machinery (Chernyavskaya et al., 2017; Chiappinelli et al., 2015; Roulois et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: In prior studies of global hypomethylation, induction of the interferon response was attributed to massive derepression of endogenous retroviral elements.
source: In each of these cases induction of the interferon response was attributed to massive derepression of endogenous retroviral elements.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of prior work.

claim: The current study identifies hypomethylation of pericentromeric sequences and derepression of associated satellite transcripts as a previously unappreciated trigger of innate immunity.
source: Our results are distinguished from these earlier studies in that we identify hypomethylation of pericentromeric sequences and subsequent derepression of associated satellite transcripts as a previously unappreciated trigger of innate immunity.
evidence: This is stated as a key distinction from prior work.

claim: Immunostimulatory motifs have been noted in pericentromeric RNAs derived from mouse and humans.
source: Immunostimulatory motifs have been noted in pericentromeric RNAs derived from mouse and humans, and transcripts derived from these repeats have been observed in p53 null mouse fibroblasts following global methylation loss (Leonova et al., 2013; Tanne et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Transcripts derived from pericentromeric repeats have been observed in p53 null mouse fibroblasts following global methylation loss.
source: Immunostimulatory motifs have been noted in pericentromeric RNAs derived from mouse and humans, and transcripts derived from these repeats have been observed in p53 null mouse fibroblasts following global methylation loss (Leonova et al., 2013; Tanne et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Prior studies suggest the potential for pericentromeric hypomethylation to drive an interferon response in diverse vertebrate species.
source: However, while these studies suggest the potential for pericentromeric hypomethylation to drive an interferon response in diverse vertebrate species, experimental evidence in support of this model has been lacking.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in prior knowledge.

claim: Experimental evidence supporting pericentromeric hypomethylation driving an interferon response has been lacking prior to this study.
source: However, while these studies suggest the potential for pericentromeric hypomethylation to drive an interferon response in diverse vertebrate species, experimental evidence in support of this model has been lacking.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in prior knowledge that this study addresses.

claim: This study demonstrates a causative link between derepression of pericentromeric RNAs and the interferon response.
source: Here we demonstrate a causative link between derepression of pericentromeric RNAs and the interferon response, and identify a requirement for Mda5/Mavs in mediating the response.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: This study identifies a requirement for Mda5/Mavs in mediating the interferon response to pericentromeric RNA.
source: Here we demonstrate a causative link between derepression of pericentromeric RNAs and the interferon response, and identify a requirement for Mda5/Mavs in mediating the response.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: Aberrant Sat1 transcripts derived from pericentromeric repeats trigger the interferon response.
source: Our findings suggest that aberrant Sat1 transcripts derived from pericentromeric repeats trigger this response, and that these transcripts may mimic features of double stranded RNA viruses in the cytosol.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: Sat1 transcripts may mimic features of double stranded RNA viruses in the cytosol.
source: Our findings suggest that aberrant Sat1 transcripts derived from pericentromeric repeats trigger this response, and that these transcripts may mimic features of double stranded RNA viruses in the cytosol.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the requirement for Mda5/Mavs.

claim: The Mda5/Mavs pathway may recognize additional endogenous RNAs that lack viral origin.
source: This finding raises the possibility that this pathway may also recognize additional endogenous RNAs that lack viral origin.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on the findings.

claim: Mutation of mda5/mavs had little impact on other ICF phenotypes observed in zbtb24 mutants.
source: While mutation of mda5/mavs rescued the interferon response in zbtb24 mutants, mda5/mavs mutation had little impact on other ICF phenotypes observed in zbtb24 mutants.
evidence: This is stated based on observation of phenotypes in double mutants.

claim: The interferon response is unlikely to drive ICF etiology.
source: Therefore, we find it unlikely that the interferon response drives ICF etiology.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of phenotype rescue in mda5/mavs; zbtb24 double mutants.

claim: The interferon response represents an additional consequence of pericentromeric hypomethylation.
source: Rather this response represents an additional consequence of pericentromeric hypomethylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the lack of phenotype rescue.

claim: Hypomethylation of pericentromeric sequences is compatible with human viability.
source: Hypomethylation of pericentromeric sequences is compatible with human viability and is observed in abnormal cell contexts including cancer and senescence.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ICF syndrome and cancer.

claim: Hypomethylation of pericentromeric sequences is observed in cancer and senescent cells.
source: Hypomethylation of pericentromeric sequences is compatible with human viability and is observed in abnormal cell contexts including cancer and senescence.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Massive increases in pericentromeric transcripts have been noted in cancer.
source: Massive increases in pericentromeric transcripts and upregulation of interferon genes have both been noted in cancer (Cheon et al., 2014; Ting et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Upregulation of interferon genes has been noted in cancer.
source: Massive increases in pericentromeric transcripts and upregulation of interferon genes have both been noted in cancer (Cheon et al., 2014; Ting et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Pericentromeric hypomethylation and subsequent derepression of associated RNAs may represent an important but underappreciated trigger of autoimmunity in a variety of disease states.
source: Our data raise the possibility that pericentromeric hypomethylation and subsequent derepression of associated RNAs represents an important but underappreciated trigger of autoimmunity in a variety of disease states.
evidence: This is stated as a broader implication of the findings.
